plot: On a snowy winter morning tiny Mouse is freezing, so Max tries to build her a snow house; fluffy snow blows away, Bird lands on the roof and it slides off, and the next house is too tiny, until Dog sits hard on a snow pile and Max discovers that packed snow makes strong bricks, so they build a cozy snow house where Mouse is warm and Dog's head fits too.

script.title: Max Builds a House Out of Snow

beats.say: Ah... ah... achoo! Brrr! Max, my whiskers are frozen like tiny icicles!
Oh no! Mouse, you are shaking like a jelly on a plate!
It is a bright winter morning. Snow covers everything, like a big white blanket.
Your fur is so thick, Max. I am so small, the wind goes right through me.
Then I will build you a house. A snow house! Snow can keep the wind out.
A house made of snow? Won't it be cold inside?
Grandma says snow houses are cozy inside. Let us try!
Max scoops up soft, fluffy snow and makes a little wall.
One wall! Easy peasy, snowy squeezy!
Then a puff of wind blows, and the fluffy wall falls into powder.
Hey! My wall turned into sugar!
Maybe it needs more snow? A much bigger pile?
Good morning, snowy friends! What are we making? A nest? I love nests!
A snow house for Mouse. Can you help us carry some snow?
Carry snow? I have wings, not buckets. But I can land on top and test it!
Max builds a big, round pile of snow. It looks like a house! Almost.
Bird lands on the very top. Plop! The whole thing slides down, with Bird inside.
I am fine! I am a snowbird now! Ha ha!
Oh dear. My house has no roof. And no walls. And no house.
Okay. This time I make it small. Small houses are strong houses.
Max makes a tiny snow house. It is so tiny that Mouse cannot fit inside.
Max, only my nose fits in here. The rest of me is still cold!
Too fluffy, too wobbly, and now too tiny. Snow houses are hard!
Snow! Snow! I love snow! Wheee!
Dog runs, slides, and sits down hard on a big pile of snow. Bump!
Oops. I made the snow all flat.
Wait, Dog! Don't move! Look at the snow under you.
Max taps the snow where Dog sat. Tap, tap. It is hard, like a brick!
When you squash snow, it gets strong! Soft snow falls down, but packed snow stays up.
So we need lots of squashing. Who is the best squasher?
Me! I am the best sitter in the whole wide world!
Dog sits on the snow. Max pats it into blocks. Bird carries tiny bits of snow in her beak.
It is a very little bit of snow, but it is my best bit!
Block by block, the walls grow. One block. Two blocks. Three blocks.
Then the round top goes on, very gently, so it does not fall.
Mouse, it is ready. Come and try your new house!
Mouse runs inside. The wind cannot reach her. The air is still and quiet.
Max! It is warm in here! Well, not hot. But so cozy!
The snow keeps the wind out, just like a thick blanket.
Can I come in too? I helped. I sat a lot.
Dog pushes his head inside. Only his head fits. His tail stays outside, wagging.
This is perfect. My head is cozy, and my tail is cool.
I will sit on the roof. Gently this time. Very, very gently.
And this time, the roof does not fall. Not even a little bit.
My goodness! A snow house! Who built this beautiful thing?
We all did, Grandma. Even Dog's bottom helped!
Packing the snow tight was very clever. And building for a friend is even better.
Thank you, Max. This is the best house I ever had.
When something does not work, try a new way. Even a Dog-sitting way!
Everyone snuggles around the snow house, and the morning sun sparkles on the walls.
Next time, we'll build a snow slide all the way down the hill!
